220170101.text: I'm done! I don't care how much you beg! I quit being a writer!

220170102.text: Archons... this is the seventh time you've threatened me with a strike... and not once was it a serious threat.

220170103.text: What are you guys fighting about this time...

220170104.text: You're finally here, Traveler! You have to help me!

220170105.text: He's been going overboard ever since you took his side the last time. He's been laying down dozens of rules for me!

220170106.text: From naming to plot design. He wants to make a set of... writing standards!

220170107.text: How am I supposed to write like this!? Why doesn't he just write it then!?

220170108.text: These are principles of writing that I've extracted from successful novels. They are tried and true guidelines.

220170109.text: That's imposing the formula of other novels onto my work. Am I writing my own novel, or am I copying someone else's?

220170110.text: I would never write so rigidly... If you want something like that, you should write it yourself!

220170111.text: Besides, aren't there already a lot of these novels rotting away in the Yae Publishing House?

220170112.text: That's just poor marketing, not the novel itself...

220170113.text: It had nothing to do with the sales strategy. It's purely because of the way those authors wrote their novels.

220170114.text: You may not know them all, but I, as an author, have read every book published by Yae Publishing House.

220170115.text: Traveler, could you get some novels for me? Shigeru and I need to have an important discussion.

220170118.text: Just bring me the novels that I keep around. I often use them as a warning to myself... of what not to write.

subQuests.subQuestName: Collect three light novels that meet the requirements

220170201.text: Traveler, could you get some novels for me? Shigeru and I need to have an important discussion.

220170202.text: Hmph. If I let him write however he pleases, he will ruin the novels for sure.

subQuests.subQuestName: Show Shigeru the correct light novel

220170301.text: Traveler, did you bring those novels? Let's have a look.

220170601.text: I think this novel has the same fantasy background as "Onibudou"...

220170602.text: Yes. The setting in this novel is very popular. The author even wrote a book just about the details of the world, and that one sold like hotcakes!

220170603.text: However, the features of the setting are presented to the reader from the very beginning and more aren't added in halfway through. Plus, it's all relevant to the plot.

220170604.text: Uh... well... Traveler, do we have any other books here...

220170401.text: I remember this one. This suspense novel was popular for a long time, wasn't it?

220170402.text: The reason for its success is because of the clever mysteries and plot structure.

220170403.text: Although many readers have said that part of the plot is impossible to follow, the author still stuck to their own principles.

220170404.text: That's why this novel stands out from other suspense novels.

220170405.text: But doesn't this novel also have a solid setting? A solid setting that isn't easily altered is the key to support the plot of this sort of suspense novel.

220170406.text: Uh... well... Traveler, do we have any other books here...

220170501.text: How about this one, then? I remember its writing was excellent and its plot was well-designed. It was highly praised by the editors. Also, its sales were excellent.

220170503.text: It was so caught up with the rigid plot and setting that it didn't have any room for expansion in the story. In the end, it just became repetitive.

220170504.text: It gradually lost readers because it lacked fresh stories. In the end, it lost all of its readers and fizzled out ignominiously.

220170505.text: Whether it's the setting or the plot, if you put yourself inside a box, all your stories will look the same. You'll stagnate.

220170506.text: I don't want my novel to be like that! The most important thing a story should have is life!

220170507.text: If... if the author himself is not interested in his own story, how can he make the reader feel that same passion?

220170510.text: I didn't know that you thought so much about these things. No wonder you wrote a novel like "Onibudou."

220170511.text: I don't want to limit your creativity, but I've seen too many authors ruin their work because of their excessive imagination...

220170512.text: Junkichi, what do you think of creativity as a writer?

220170513.text: I believe that it's the desire to create. A writer who has no desire to create won't be able to write words that attract readers.

220170514.text: In my opinion, it's more important still for a writer to exercise restraint in expressing that creative desire.

220170518.text: But I'm not the author of this novel. You are. I'm just an editor who needs to help you finish it.

220170519.text: If you insist on your ideas, then create them as you wish.

220170520.text: I can't say that I agree with you. But I will try to understand you.

220170522.text: You're welcome. Of course, I get where you're coming from. But you need to understand my position, too. For example...

220170524.text: For example, it's been another day, where is your manuscript!?

220179901.text: This one's called "The Sage Aetolia Will Die Tomorrow." A really impressive name. Long-winded, too...

220179902.text: This one's "The Honest Cat's Little Lie"... Hmm, Paimon wonders what it's about?

220179903.text: This one's name is "Literature Club." What a simple and short name...

220179904.text: Paimon wonders which of these three novels Junkichi wants. Well, we might as well take them all to him.
